reviews:
[{"text":"In 1988, POLTERGEIST III was release to an audience worldwide, for one more round of frightning ghosts.

STEVEN and DIANE FREELING have sent CAROL ANNE (again played by Heather O'Rourke, in her last starring role) to live with Diane's sister PAT GARDENER (played by Nancy Allen) and Pat's husband, BRUCE GARDENER (played by the brilliant Tom Skerritt) in the urban city of Chicago, Illinois. Pat and Bruce also have an 18-year-old daughter named DONNA (played by Lara Flynn Boyle). Carol Anne seems to be adjusting to the city very well, but she is feeling homesick, and misses her family very much. She goes to a school for the gifted. The school's psychiatrist, DR. SEATON (played by Richard Fire) as put Carol Anne under hypnosis, making her relive the memories of her terrifying ordeal with Reverend Kane. Dr. Seaton seems to think that this just in Carol Anne's head, but KANE (played by Nathan Davis) has returned to claim Carol Anne once again.

That night, Pat and Bruce head off to an opening part at Pat's new Art Gallery, which is located in the huge Chicago Skyscraper building (both Bruce and Pat work in the building, as well as live in it). Donna is to be babysitting Carol Anne, but knowing that Donna wants to go to her friends' party (who also live in the building), Carol Anne tells Donna to go on ahead to the party. But as Donna leaves, Carol Anne is visited by Kane in a terrifying meeting. At the moment, TANGINA BARRONS (again played by Zelda Rubenstein), who already is on her way to Carol Anne's aid, gives Carol Anne a telepathic message. Carol Anne runs around the garage of the building, where she then steps on a puddle, where the spirits jump up through the puddle grabbing Carol Anne. Donna and her boyfriend, SCOTT (played by Kipley Wentz) are in the security room trying to rig it up, so that they and their friends could have a few hours in the pool, but Donna finds Carol Anne, where she and Scott run to Carol Anne, but the three are pulled into the puddle, and are taken to the other side, where they are between dimensions: they are on the other side of every mirror in the building. Pat and Bruce run up to find Scott shivering and terrified, where Pat and Bruce run up to Carol Anne's bedroom. Carol Anne busts through her door, with Pat trying to pull her out, but Tangina arrives and pushes Pat and Bruce out of the way, informing them that Carol Anne and Donna are not in the room, but on the other side, between dimensions. They find out where Carol Anne and Donna were captured, where Tangina, Bruce, and Pat find Carol Anne in the reflection of the mirror, but the reflection of Carol Anne is Kane in disguise, where he then takes Tangina to other side. Out of the corpse-like body of Tangina (what she turned into after she was taken where Carol Ann and Donna are), Donna comes out of the body, but apparently, this is not Donna, and Scott (who came out of the pool) is not Scott, but some of Kane's disciples in disguise. Pat and Bruce run all over trying to save the girls. They find Tangina, who hands them her necklace (an amulet if you will), where she informs them that Kane is controlling the inside of the building, but not the outside. Bruce and Pat, on a cherry picker, ride up to Carol Anne's window. Bruce hands Pat the necklace, where he enters the bedroom. She sees Carol Anne, where she tells Pat to forget about her, and save Bruce and Donna, but once again, Kane has taken Carol Anne's appearance. Pat enters the room, and has an outing with Kane, until Tangina, who is still on the other side, informs Kane that he does not need Carol Anne to lead him into the light. Tangina takes Kane and leads him into the light. Where Bruce, Donna, and Carol Anne return. Carol Anne's nightmare is over.

This was definitely an excellent sequel, and a great way to end the Poltergeist trilogy. Sadly, Heather O'Rourke, the actress who played CAROL ANNE in all three films, sadly passed on in February of 1988, at the tender age of 12. She died just before the film was completed. But the crew decided to finish the film, in honor of Heather O'Rourke. The ending had to be changed, which is why when Tom Skerritt is holding Carol Anne, you never see Carol Anne look up from Tom's shoulder. This is a great film, and we should all keep Heather O'Rourke in our hearts, since she did such a wonderful job playing the character that won our hearts in all three of these films.

R.I.P.
Heather O'ROURKE
(1975-1988)","rating":5,"timestamp":1106174152000}]

reviews:
[{"text":"Linda Blair reprises her role as Regan MacNeil, who this time is staying with her former nanny, Sharon, in New York, and is seeing Dr. Jean Tuskin, the owner of a hospital for gifted children. When Tuskin begins suspecting Regan hasn't been telling all she remembers about the former trauma in Washington, Father Lamont arrives and begins investigating - and with the help of Regan, things might just get a little more interesting. Or not...for this film, including some decent special effects and photography, is just plain bad. The acting is bad, the script is lacking in any sort of feeling or realism, and the story overall is just terrible. Ennio Morricone's musical score is eerie, but that's really the only thing that stands out in this otherwise dreary, horrible film.","rating":2.0,"timestamp":1059968693000},{"text":"1973's THE EXORCIST is widely known as \\"The Scariest Movie Of All Time\\". Everything about that film scares the living daylights out of every human being on God's green earth. In 1977, a sequel to the film was released. That sequel is entitled, EXORCIST II: THE HERETIC.

It has been four years since Regan's possession and exorcism, since the sudden death of Father Merrin and Father Karras, both who performed Regan's exorcism. REGAN MacNEIL (again played by Linda Blair) is now 16, and doing fine, or she seems to be. She is having nightmares about her terrifying ordeal that had happened four years earlier. She seeks the psychiatric help of DR. GENE TUSKIN (played by Louise Fletcher). Regan is here only to make her mother (who does not appear in this film) feel better, only because of her divorce and busy career as an actress.

Elsewhere, FATHER PHILIP LAMONT (played by Richard Burton) has gotten back from Spain, where he performed an exorcism on a young girl. The exorcism didn't go well, for the girl had sadly died from her demonic possession. But the Cardinal has given Father Lamont a new assignment: Investigate the death of Father Lankester Merrin. He tracks down Regan at the psychiatric institute, where she and Dr. Tuskin hold their sessions.

As Father Lamont arrives, Dr. Tuskin informs Regan of a new machine that can help Regan's therapy. Regan claims that she remembers nothing of her possession and exorcism. This machine puts Regan under hypnosis and relaxtion, where Dr. Tuskin can go under with Regan and see her memories, that Regan claims to not remember.

The next day is when Dr. Tuskin and Regan have their first session with the machine, but it causes Dr. Tuskin's heart to filbertrate, where Father Lamont has to go under and help Dr. Tuskin out. What she and Father Lamont saw was the exorcism four years ago. It showed how Regan (possessed) killed Father Merrin. Through the hypnosis, Father Lamont kept hearing the name...PAZUZU. Apparently, Pazuzu is the name of the demon that had possessed Regan four years earlier.

Father Lamont continues his investigation, by going under hypnosis with Regan. The hypnosis takes Father Lamont to Africa, where he sees Father Merrin's first exorcism, that was mentioned in the first film, four years earlier. Pazuzu had taken possession of a young African boy named KOKUMO.

That night, Regan has another nightmare. SHARON SPENCER (again played by Kitty Winn) comes to Regan's bedroom, trying to find out what's wrong, but she finds Regan up a little earlier than usual. Sharon is the young woman who lived with Regan and Chris in the first film. Now, Sharon and Regan lived together. Sharon informs Regan that she's flying over to Washington, and won't be home when Regan comes home from school.

Sharon arrives in Washington, and meets with Father Lamont at Regan's old house. She shows Father Lamont around, where it all happened. I was rather creeped out with this scene, knowing that it was the original house, where Regan's exorcism took place. Father Lamont is told by Sharon to go upstairs to Regan's old bedroom to see where Regan had been while under the possession, where the exorcism took place.

Father Lamont has another session with Regan, where he finds, through hypnosis, where KOKUMO (played by James Earl Jones). After the session, Father Lamont goes off to Africa to have a meeting with Kokumo.

While in Africa, Father Lamont shows FATHER ABBOTT (an African priest) where one of his monks had died, during Kokumo's possession, but they fear Father Lamont to be a Devil-worshipper, where they through rocks at him. Regan, because of how many times she and Father Lamont have gone under hypnosis together, feels the pain, where she ends up in the hospital overnight.

Father Lamont reaches Kokumo, where Kokumo tells him of how the rubbing of the wings of two grasshoppers is what causes the transformation of grasshopper to locust. He informs Father Lamont to rip out Regan's evil heart.

He returns to the states and meets Regan at a museum, where she steals the hypnosis machine and takes off. They reach an appartment, where they see Father Merrin again. But Father Lament, through a slight trance, takes off to Penn Station, where Regan follows. The two are headed for Washington, where they'll be going to Regan's old house, to defeat Pazuzu once and for all. She calls Dr. Tuskin right away, where she and Sharon go on their way, following both Regan and Father Lamont.

They reach the house and head upstairs, but as Father Lamont opens the door to Regan's old bedroom, a sworm of Locusts surround Father Lamont. At that same time, the cab that Dr. Tuskin and Sharon are in swirves out a control and crashes into the front gate of Regan's house. Dr. Tuskin gets out and tries to get inside, but Sharon, while standing on gasoline, lights herself on fire. Upstairs, Regan and Father Lamont open the bedroom door again to find the apparition of Regan's possessed body, where it transforms into Regan's current appearance. It begins forcing Father Lamont to kill Regan, but through a psychiatric trance, Regan has Father Lamont attack the spirit and rip out the evil heart, where the house crumbles to the ground. Regan and Father Lamont make it out safely and approach Sharon and Dr. Tuskin. Sharon is burnt pretty badly and is almost at death, where she apologizes for choosing evil, and then dies.

We all know for a fact that no sequel or remake will ever out-do THE EXORCIST, but this sequel was done very well. Yeah, it is not that scary, and it is not the predecessor, but in my own opinion (please don't slam me for this because it is my opinion, and my opinion alone), this sequel was very good.","rating":4.0,"timestamp":1156391524000}]

Every time they see this movie they clap at the end; they shout cheers and exclaim “That is how it is done!” This movie has won 5 Academy Awards, and they are: Best Picture, Best Actor in a Leading Role which was Russell Crowe, Best Costume Design, Best Sound, and Best Effects and Visual Effects. This movie was directed by Ridley Scott and the movie is an epic historical action drama. It stars Russell Crowe, Joaquin Phoenix, Connie Nielsen, and more that made this movie bring the audience back to see it again and again! Hurrah for Ridley Scott, hurrah for a great cast and with an amazing wardrobe and set designer!
A Roman gladiator stands at the center of the great colosseum looking up at the emperor, awaiting his decision. With the power of life and death in his hands, all the emperor has to do is stretch out his arm and put his thumb up for life or down for death. This was the scene, captured in the painting called “Thumbs Down” by Jean-Leon Gerome that fired up the director Ridley Scott and put him at the helm of this movie “Gladiator.” “The image spoke to me of the Roman Empire in all its glory and wickedness. I knew right then and there I was hooked,” says Ridley. “Gladiator” did not only hook Ridley, but thousands of people who have seen this movie. Scott has directed a number of great movies such as Alien, Blade Runner, Kingdom of Heaven, Robin Hood, and Gladiator just to name a few of his great movies. Scotts movies are great influences for anyone who has seen them. Scott and his crew for the movie knew that they had to find an actor who could be this Gladiator who could fulfill their idea of this movie and Russell Crowes name came up quite quickly.
Each actor played their parts with greatness! Russell Crowe played the leading role of Maximus. Maximus was a general who fought for Rome to expand the empire at the Emperors request. Douglas Wick was the man who picked Russell Crowe to play the leading role of Maximus. “Maximus is the very soul of the movie,” Wick states. Crowes facial expressions matched every scene perfectly. When he was fighting, he shouted, yelled, and if hurt his face showed it; when he saw his home destroyed and family butchered, he wept and drooled. Joaquin Phoenix played the co-star role of Commodus who hated Maximus. He was the emperors’ son and was expecting his father to name him as the new emperor but he did not name him the emperor, he named maximus. Phoenix’ face shows great hurt and distrust of his father when he names Maximus the new emperor, and great rage. With his rage he killed his father, and ordered that Maximus be killed and all of his family. Throughout the movie he shows hatred for Maximus when he finds out that Maximus has become the great gladiator that the whole city of Rome is talking about. His sister, Lucilla, is played by Connie Nielsen. She is in love with Maximus and wants to free him from being a gladiator. She shows in her face the love and adoration she has for him and tried to save him. She also is afraid of her brother and not only proclaims that but shows that by telling her bother everything that she had been planning with Maximus. All three of them made the audience believe that this was based on a true story; that is how good the acting was!
During the reign of the Roman Empire, about two thousand years ago, people dressed differently then the way people do today. During peace time people usually wore a type of robe, something similar to a cloak, and the color of it was dark brown to light brown if the person waring it was a peasant, but if the person was royalty the cloak would be purple. During times of war the soldiers wore armor and fought with swords and spears, not like today when most wars are fought with guns. Janty Yates is the brilliant creator for the wardrobe of all the actors from all scenes of the movie. She came up with what the armor of maxims looked like, what clothes a princess would ware, and even what weapons to use while the fighting was in the arena. She won the Academy Award for best costume design for Gladiator! She knows what clothes, weapons, and armor it takes to win.
All good things must come to an end, and the movie goes out with a big bang! I’m giving you a heads up for the spoiler alert, so after the last battle between Commodus and Maximus, both of them die, but not at the same time. Maxims kills Commodus with a small dagger that Commodus used to stab Maximus in his back earlier before their fight. After Commodus falls, Maximus speaks with a Republican of the people Senator Gracchus played by Derek Jacobi. He tells Gracchus that the emperor wanted to give Rome back to the people before he was slain in the beginning of the movie by Commodus.
